note: How a recognisable thing is assembled from Build primitives, and what was seen when it was. Each record keeps three kinds of statement apart: `native` (read from engine source or map fields), `derived` (counted by a named tool) and `interpreted` (what a viewer took it for, with who the viewer was). `status` is the weakest link: `observed_once` means one build in one context; `transferred` means it held in a second context that differs in size, material and surroundings; `refuted` records stay, with what refuted them. A record is corrected by adding a `supersedes` entry, never by rewriting.

records.appearance: a building that is visibly taller or lower than its neighbours
native: A one-sided wall is drawn from its own sector's floor to its own sector's ceiling.
The upper section of a two-sided wall is skipped when both sectors have parallax ceilings (NBlood/source/build/src/engine.cpp:4688), so a step between two skies paints nothing.
The ceiling still clips the player and sprites whether or not it is drawn.
records.construction: Put a strip of open ground (an apron) against the face and give it the sky height the face should be drawn to. `bloodmap.skyline.apron`. One sector per distinct height; no change in plan.
constraints: Nothing shows over an apron's wall: the wall is one-sided and what is painted above it is the apron's own sky. A tower set back behind a lower front paints no pixel. For depth, the campaign's other technique is needed: a roof sector with a raised floor (E1M5: seven wall heights, no sky step).
Where two aprons of different height meet at an inside corner the seam must be a diagonal from the corner, or one sector owns both faces and draws one of them wrong.
The apron's sky must be out of reach: `skyline.REACH`, three bodies.

interpreted.said: grey block steps up into a taller plain shaft, could be a tower (guess)
roofline with sky over it; tower visible from the spawn and the market end

records.transfer: Held in a second context inside the same experiment: the churchyard wall (different tile 417, 3.1 bodies, 4096 and 6144 long, no building behind it) and the tower (17.4 bodies, sloped). Not yet tried in another map or district.

refuted_by.by: owner, playing the build in NBlood
refuted_by.said: when you put parallax sky low it is covering view like a normal ceiling
refuted_by.evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/church-roofs/before: yard_to_tower (the tower paints 0 px), yard_out_south, avenue_over_wall
refuted_by.what_survives: the native facts are true, and RAISING a sky for the one thing taller than the city is sound. Lowering one is what is refuted. See 'height-is-a-raised-floor'.

records.appearance: a wall, a building or a roof that is lower than what stands beyond it, with what stands beyond it still visible over it
native: A low parallax ceiling is painted from the top of the far wall upward over every column its sector covers; it occludes exactly like a roofed ceiling.
The lower step of a two-sided wall is drawn from the wall record on the lower side, so a raised sector's face takes its tile from its neighbour's wall.

derived.note: most campaign maps with varied wall heights have no sky step of a body or more; the heights come from floors

records.construction: The low thing is a sector whose floor is its top, under the common sky: `bloodmap.skyline.roof`, then `skyline.dress_steps` to paint its face from the side that sees it. Over an interior it is its own layer with a band clear of the rooms beneath.

interpreted.said: cemetery wall (guess); 'nothing here says cemetery'
graveyard / cemetery (certain); yard_to_tower 'the most church-like frame'

records.transfer: Held across three different things in one build: a boundary wall with no building behind it (tile 417, 3.1 bodies), a building's low range over an interior (406, 3.9) and a pitched nave over that (sloped floor, 5.8 to 7.0). Not yet in another map.

records.appearance: (a fault) a room's ceiling painted into the sky beside or above a door
native: The classic renderer keeps one open span per screen column (umost/dmost). Columns above a low two-sided wall stay open; a sector reached meanwhile through any portal paints into them.
bloodmap/layers.py states the same law for storeys: the space you enter the ground floor from must not also open into the storey above it through the same facade.
records.construction: Put the way in under something nothing is seen over: a tower or a full-height block, whose one-sided walls close the columns they cover and whose entry room lies inside its plan. Put a second door between that room and the rooms under the roof, and let both shut themselves (`doors.z_motion_door(close_after=30)`). `skyline.leaks_under_roofs(layout)` finds the violations on the source.

interpreted.said: 'a thin dark pole', 'a sky-length seam' in five frames
took it for the sky tile's painted spires

constraints: Measured in the observer, which is JFBuild's software renderer. NBlood's default renderer is not, and was not tested for this.
The auto-close is a mitigation: with both doors held open the leak is there.
records.transfer: Not tried elsewhere. The law is the engine's and should hold; the cure has been built once.

records.appearance: sky visible over a building at a level gaze
native: The observer's vertical half-field at 640x480 is about 30 degrees; z is a sixteenth of xy.

derived.prediction_that_failed: sky share in avenue_front would rise by 0.15 with the eaves at 6.8 bodies

records.construction: On a street W wide, what fronts the street must be lower than about 0.6 W (in xy units; multiply by 16 for z) for its top to show from the far kerb. On Gravesend's 7-unit avenue that is about 3.9 bodies. Taller things are skyline for the long view down the street, not for the facade view.

interpreted.said: the height that matters on a street is the height of what fronts it; a church's low side range, not its nave

records.transfer: Untested elsewhere. It is geometry, so it should hold; the 30-degree figure is the observer's and NBlood's field of view may differ.

records.appearance: a tower that ends in a point rather than a flat top
native: A sector has one ceiling plane; a sloped parallax ceiling tilts the top edge of every wall drawn against it.
Build has no pyramid: a spire is not sayable with walls and one slope per sector.
records.construction: Split the apron on each tower face at the face's centre line; hinge each half on that line and let it fall toward the corner. Mitre the corners. Six sectors for a tower with three street faces.

interpreted.by: blind reviewer, round 2 (gable 1.9 bodies on a 15.5-body shaft)
interpreted.said: no spire, reads as a chimney / obelisk

interpreted.by: blind reviewer, round 3 (gable 3.9 bodies, ridge 17.4), far views
interpreted.said: church steeple (certain as a silhouette)

interpreted.by: blind reviewer, round 3, from the tower's foot
interpreted.said: a plain square shaft, ends flat against the sky; the steeple seen from afar does not match the tower seen up close
wrote 'reads as a steeple' from the far frames and was half wrong; see critic-round3.md

constraints: A gable under about a quarter of the shaft's visible height is foreshortened to nothing from the street.
Even a steep gable does not show from the tower's own foot: the far read (silhouette) and the near read (what is at eye height) are separate problems. Gables solve the first only.
evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/church-skyline/round2 and after: vista_far, spawn_north, avenue_south_up, tower_foot
records.transfer: Not tried in a second context. The near read is unsolved.

records.appearance: a stone building recognised as a church
native: Tile 569 is 32x32, four vertical panes; E1M5 uses it as a masked two-sided wall 512 wide at x_repeat 4, y_repeat 8 between an alcove and the sky.
records.construction: Where the wall is one-sided, hang 569 as a wall sprite: x_repeat 48, y_repeat 192 gives a lancet 384 wide and 1.45 bodies tall. One per bay, between buttresses.

interpreted.by: blind reviewer, round 1 (massing only, no glass)
interpreted.said: civic or warehouse block (guess); fortress (guess)

interpreted.by: blind reviewer, round 2 (same massing lowered, buttresses, glass)
interpreted.said: church/chapel (likely) -- 'purely from the coloured glass'
church (likely), 'but only because of the glass'

constraints: This is an ablation by history, not a controlled one: round 2 changed eaves height, buttresses and glass together. The reviewer named the glass as the cue; that is one reviewer.
A sprite is flat. From hard against the wall it reads as paint. E1M5's real glazed opening does not.
records.transfer: Not tried. Promote only after a second building and a controlled removal of the glass alone.

records.appearance: a long wall given bays and depth
native: A notch in a sector's outline is three walls and no sector.
records.construction: Let small rectangles into the apron's outline against the face: 256 proud, 384 wide, on the bay grid, flanking the portal. They stand exactly as tall as the eaves because they are walls of the same sector.

interpreted.said: pilasters either side of the door; top reads as 'a flat crenellated line', fortress or warehouse

constraints: Because each buttress carries the facade tile's cornice round its own top, the roofline steps at every one and reads as battlements. A buttress that stops below the eaves needs its own lower apron.

records.appearance: a shop window that reads as glass set into a wall
native: A wall record has one x_repeat/y_repeat; it scales the record's masked middle and its upper and lower step bands alike (AlignWalls, xmapedit/src_blood/xmpmaped.cpp:3024-3050).
A two-sided wall's step bands are drawn from the record on the side that sees them.
derived: Gravesend before: 24 of 24 glazed records also carried a step band; 8 were street records. One 1024-long pane's facade band was drawn at 4x the facade's scale, a 7168 one at 0.57x.
After: 0 of 20 carry a band, 0 are street records; `collinear solid-portal` joins that continue in x rose from 85% to 97% (tools.texture_continuity).
records.construction: From the street inward: a reveal, one sash pocket per bay with solid mullions between, a display box, the shop. Reveal, sashes and box share one floor and one ceiling. The street-side record is two-sided to the reveal and carries the facade's lintel and stall riser at the facade's scale. The pane hangs between a sash and the box. `glass.shopfront` in blood-city gives the rectangles; `bloodmap.glass.glaze(fit=True)` keeps E6M1's glass density on a pane of any length.

interpreted.said: the glass should sit in a aperure/frame so glass texture scaling won't be colliding with facade texture
the glass is set into the wall: a recess, mullions or posts, a sill ledge and a dark frame; the other set looks laid flat on the wall, one pale rain-streaked sheet

constraints: A mullion must not reach the street face, where it would be a full-height slice of the facade's painted windows: the reveal runs unbroken in front of the sashes.

E6M1 itself hangs its pane between the recess and the shop, with the sill under the glass: that record has a band. `bloodmap.glass.recess_faults` accepts both arrangements by asking the whole frame for a sill.
records.transfer: Three venues built three ways (theatre, market hall, arcade) took the one helper. Not tried outside this city.

records.appearance: a dado at the floor, a facade's ground storey at the pavement, a kerb one tile tall
native: GetWallZPeg (xmpmaped.cpp:2991-3022): a one-sided wall hangs from its ceiling; a two-sided one from the top step's ceiling, then the bottom step's floor.
A texel is 2048 / y_repeat z tall.
derived: Tile 2294 is 32x256: plaster over a rail and a tiled dado in its bottom 100 rows. In the market hall (192 rows tall) the run's vertical origin was the first wall's peg, a window head: the dado was drawn under the ceiling and never at the floor.
Tile 6 (owner: kerb) is 64x8: at y_repeat 8 it is exactly E3M1's 2048 kerb.
records.construction: `bloodmap.texture_frame.frame_map(v_anchor='floor')`: one vertical origin per run, the z at which the tile's bottom row lies on the floor most of the run stands on. Every join that continued still continues.

interpreted.said: Be careful abount meaningful texture aligment, it seems like a thing that is sometimes off

hall band: 'patchy ... red tile over some openings and plain grey plaster over others ... unfinished'; preferred the old continuous crate frieze 'narrowly' while calling it 'crate art used as wall trim'

constraints: It is a city-wide change of phase: every interior frame changed, the church's included, though nothing in the church was touched.
A tile with a cornice at its top and a base at its bottom fits only a wall a whole number of tiles tall. Floor wins.
A facade tile used on something that is not a facade shows a different slice once anchored: the market stalls' edges turned from cornice to brick, which is how that fault was found.
records.transfer: Applied to the whole city in one pass. Not tried on another map; the zoo still uses the editor's first-wall anchor.

records.appearance: the band over an opening continuing the room's wall
native: Build draws a two-sided wall's upper step from that wall's own picnum.
derived: tools.mine_apertures.dominant_wall_tile took the commonest picnum per wall record, portals included. The market hall has 16 crate rims 1024 long and 11,776 units of plaster: 'facade' came out as crate (452), and blood-city's lintel pass painted 24,064 units of band with it.
records.construction: The facade is the sector's one-sided wall, weighed by length; two-sided records only when it has no solid wall.

interpreted.said: these ceiling crates doesn't feel right

constraints: The campaign aperture census in apertures-v1.json was computed with the old definition and has not been re-run.

records.appearance: a street where you can tell the walk from the road
native: The lower step of a two-sided wall is drawn from the lower side's record: a kerb's face is the carriageway's wall.
derived: E3M1 and E6M1: paving 4 over cobble 352, 2048 step, tile 6 on the road side (13 walls). Owner-anchored as stone paving, cobblestone, kerb.
The campaign dresses its city street with geometry, not sprites: E3M1 has 6 decoration sprites outdoors in the whole map.
Campaign street lamps (2493, E2) stand 256 off the facade, not at the kerb, 1100-2500 apart in a cluster.
records.construction: District street floor = paving; `streets.lay` cuts cobble carriageways 2048 down wearing tile 6 on their own walls. A carriageway that lies on or across a district seam is a NOTCH in each street's outline, not a hole in one: the parts are rooms of their own districts joined across the seam, and every join (street to street, part to street, part to part) is a gate written from the finished shapes. Each run reaches a junction's depth past its end nodes, so roads meet edge to edge. The clear space is found as maximal rectangles, longest first.

interpreted.said: pavement, raised kerb, cobble road and lamps, 'the clearest street read in either set'; the old set: 'you can almost never tell'
'a grey stripe down the middle of the road ... pavement should never be a stripe down the road'

interpreted.by: second blind reviewer, centred roads with paved crossings
interpreted.said: 'a clean central road, kerbs on both sides and lamps ... the best street frame'; junctions: 'the avenue's road ends at a kerb. That reads as an error: carts would hit a kerb'
asked for the road down the middle rather than on one side of the seam

constraints: A hole may not touch its street's outline; a road on a seam must be a notch. `Room.faces` resolves at compile time, so the outline can be replaced after other code has named the street's faces, but any face used with `at=`/`width=` must be re-derived.
A guillotine tiling of the street minus its obstacles is not the clear space: it loses the full-width stretch beyond an obstacle on one side.
A run ends at a junction's centre. Two roads that stop at their nodes leave the junction to nobody.
Anything raised in a street is drawn from the street's record and wears the facade unless dressed: `skyline.dress_steps(only_from=street sectors)`.
Plazas and lanes are one paved surface; both reviewers count that as still unseparated.
A camera pose exactly on a kerb line is in no sector and the observer writes no frame, silently.

records.appearance: the far end of a street: a building face a few storeys tall with sky over it
native: A one-sided wall of a parallax sector is drawn to that sector's sky height.
A sector whose floor and ceiling are at one z draws no wall.
Where both sectors of a two-sided wall are parallax the upper step is not drawn (engine.cpp:4688).
E3M1 s340 and s338: floor 8192, ceiling 8192, ceiling_stat 3, behind the end masses s0 and s339.
E3M1 end-wall faces: facade tile at shade -8, cstat 1; the masonry beside them 24 to 34.
derived: E3M1's three end masses stand 3.86 to 5.80 bodies over the road, floor tile 379 (bloodmap.street.end_wall).
Gravesend before: 184,320 units of perimeter masonry drawn 11.6 bodies tall; the avenue is 57,000 units long.
records.construction: A mass across the street's mouth, outside the map's edge, 5.8 bodies up under the common sky, faced in the district facade (the face is the street's record: dress it, light it to -8, make it blocking). Behind it a parallax sector of no height at grade. `streets.end_walls`; `bloodmap.skyline.is_sky_backing`.

interpreted.by: blind reviewer, faces not yet lit
interpreted.said: before: 'a tall black slab ... a void or an unlit box'; after: 'the ends read as buildings across the street', far ones 'low enough to read as distant, unlit buildings under the sky. Not good, but not slabs'
'the facades look pasted onto' the masonry either side; 'the street just stops against a picture of a building'

constraints: It is the opposite of a lowered sky and must not be reported as one: a backing hides nothing because it is put where nothing stands. `lowered_skies` and the open-neighbours rule exempt a sector of no height.
Unlit, at 30,000 units, the end wall is still a dark block, only shorter. The sky does the work at distance; the lit face does it up close.
A mouth that lies in two districts is two masses, each in its own district's facade. That read as two buildings.
Nobody walks onto it: the geometry audit needs `declared_zero_exit`.
records.transfer: Four street ends in one city. Not tried elsewhere, and not on the rest of the perimeter.

records.appearance: a shopfront that says what it is
native: The step bands of a two-sided wall are drawn from the record on the side that sees them.
A region that states its own floor, ceiling or wall shade is protected from LightBomb unless its intent lists that surface under generated_surfaces (planar_layout).
derived: Rooms behind glass against the street floor, by shade: DukCity3 24 and 37; E3M1 24 and 32; Gravesend 32 and 32 before, about 21 and 32 after.
Letter sprites outdoors per map: DukCity 38 to 73, E1M4 33, E3M1 0.
A campaign sign letter hangs a median 2.54 bodies over the street (range 1.69 to 5.13); a fascia 0.72 body over a head at 1.45 puts it at 1.81.
records.construction: Give the window's reveal the street's floor and a ceiling a fascia over the window's head: the bands under and over each pane are then the reveal's own record (riser and fascia in the shop's material), the wall between two sashes is a pilaster, and the street's record over the mouth is still the facade's. Letter the name on the fascia. Hang a lamp in the display over a declared source and mark the display's and the shop's surfaces as generated. `glass.surround`, `write_names`, `hang_lamps`, `stand_pilasters` (blood-city level).

interpreted.said: sign: 'decisive. It turns the pawn from a dress shop into a pawnbroker and the super from a storeroom into a grocer'; surround: 'helps ... the sign has nothing to sit on'; unlit: 'hurts, mildly ... it hides the goods'
'The pawn's goods say boutique, not pawn'; 'the mall units sell nothing'

constraints: A lamp at an indoor bracket's strength in a room that states its shade lights nothing.
A chain lamp of fixed length hangs at eye level in a low display: cut it to the display.
The lintel pass takes a sector's solid wall for its facade: stand the pilasters after it, or one pilaster outvotes two jambs and repaints the surround.
Lettering sized for a fascia is not legible from across a street.
records.transfer: Three venues built three ways took one helper. The name-first ordering has not been tried on a venue that is not a shop.

records.appearance: a barred strongroom in a shop's back wall
native: A masked wall's overlay shares its record's scale with that record's step bands, bars as much as glass.
derived: Per interior, medians: E3M1 15.5 floor heights over 2.96 bodies, 10.5 ceiling heights, 14.5 wall tiles, 37 shade steps between darkest and brightest floor; Gravesend 7.5, 1.45, 5.5, 7.5 and 7.5 (tools/city_profile.py --interiors).
The pawn shop's interior before and after the pledge room: floor heights 5 and 5, range 0.48 and 0.48 body, ceiling heights 3 and 4, wall tiles 10 and 13, shade spread 17 and 18.
records.construction: A recess at the strongroom's own floor and ceiling, a step up from the shop, with a blocking masked wall (`bloodmap.glass.grille`, the owner's grate 463) between recess and room; the room lit, lower-ceilinged, in its own material, with goods on its back wall.

interpreted.said: goods inside: 'decisive. It turns a jail cell into a shop's secure stock'; bars removed: 'helps depth and legibility, and hurts the pawn-cage identity'; light: 'barely'
'The room is ONE flat box ... flat even light everywhere, no level change, no shadowed corner, no light source and no pool of light'

constraints: It moves none of the measures that separate these interiors from the campaign's: a small room on one wall adds a ceiling height and some tiles.
Piercing a wall changes which wall is 'the longest solid one'; anything placed by that rule moves. The shop's sign left every view.
A cage nothing meets and nobody can open reads as decoration.

records.appearance: a room that says what it is for without a sign
native: Blood's goods are breakable 'thing' sprites (types 416 and 417, status 4, cstat 385): blocking, hitscan-sensitive, one-sided face sprites.
derived: Distinct decoration tiles: Gravesend 38 before, 85 after; E3M1 61, E1M4 104, E1M2 109, DWE3M1 142 (tools/mine_city_assets.py).
335 decoration tiles across seven of Blood's town maps; 119 in two or more that Gravesend did not use.
records.construction: A plan by place (`goods.py`): things on furniture that is already geometry (a bar, a card table, a counter, a display, an altar), things on a room's wall, printed matter on a street's wall, things on a yard's ground. Each tile set down with the fields the town maps give it (`references/city-assets.json`). Run after the venues' own wall compositions.

interpreted.said: the saloon bare: 'could be a sauna, a forge or a crypt'; dressed: 'bar or saloon, likely'. 'Props on counters and tables: decisive.' 'Altar dressing: decisive for church versus crypt.'
'It is a small kit ... Interiors get 1 to 3 props each'; 'shops have no fixtures'

constraints: A tile read off its picture can be wrong in place: 505 looked like a waste bin and is a bucket of gore. It stood at three doors until a stranger saw it.
Where a view has lettering, objects only confirm it; where it has none, only objects can say what the place is.
A wall-placement pass run before a venue's own composition takes its wall.
Goods need something to stand ON: on a display's floor they read as lumps.

records.appearance: a shop or a bar where the stock is on something
native: A sprite's z is not its foot; the foot is the tile's height and y offset below it.
derived: Seven town maps, indoor standing decoration by what is under it (tools/mine_stands.py): 91 thing-carrying fixtures, median rise 0.48 body, top tile 34 on 35; a niche is 0.75 x 2.0 player widths with its head 0.72 body under the room's.
Gravesend before and after: island rise 0.18 and 0.43; share of things on a ledge or in a niche 15% and 44%.
records.construction: `fixtures.BAR` (one piece, 8192 high, top 34, face 28) and `fixtures.shelf_niche` (a recess in a wall with void behind it: floor 8192 up, 12288 clear, 384 deep), stocked by `goods.ROWS` at a thing every 340 units. A counter stops `templates.COUNTER_PASS` short of one wall.

interpreted.said: 'Back-bar or back shelf stocked with goods ... decisive. It is the single thing that turns these boxes from room with a counter into a specific trade'; empty: 'a dark slatted hole ... unfinished'
'The four shops are one kit'; 'the bookshop has no books'; 'the sign is currently doing all the work'

constraints: A counter too high to step over shuts whatever is behind it: here the level's key.
A shelf is a portal: anything placed on 'a solid wall' moves unless the rule knows how high the opening is.
A niche needs void behind the wall.
records.transfer: Not tried outside the saloon and the arcade.

records.appearance: a thing standing on a floor, a counter or a shelf; a sign on a wall
native: engine.cpp setup_globals_sprite1: bottom = z - yoff*yrepeat*4, plus half the height when cstat bit 128 is set; top = bottom - height*yrepeat*4.
db.h GetSpriteExtents (physics) ignores bit 128. The two boxes agree only when the bit is set.
derived: Seven town maps: for standing tiles 712, 739, 1009, 1013, 3540 the median z over the floor equals the drawn box's bottom to within 8 units.
Share of sprites drawn over a tenth under their floor: town maps 0% to 2.1%; Gravesend 5.2% before, 0% after. Wall-sprite pairs covering each other: E3M1 1, E1M2 6, Gravesend 16 before, 1 after.
Tile 640 outdoors in DWE3M1: 18 of 26 at repeat 120 (2.1 bodies), median 512 from the kerb's edge, median 8,192 to the next. E3M1 has none.
records.construction: `bloodmap.placement.drawn_extent` / `drawn_lift`; `goods.put_floor` refuses a thing that hangs in the town maps, is taller than its place, wider than its row, or is floor-only on a fixture; `tools/sprite_fit.py` lints the built map.

interpreted.said: 'sprites partially under ground or into space where they don't fit ... statues on weird places ... lamps placed little bit weirdly ... overlapping sprites, usually letters with other sprites'
'M is clearly better'; before: 'statues ... crammed into the shelf', 'lettering on top of art', lamps 'miniature'

constraints: The lint knows geometry, not meaning: what belongs where is still a rule someone wrote.
An actor's picture in the map is not what the game draws.
records.transfer: The lint runs on any Blood map.
